run.question: The payment-api pod in namespace app-259 had issues on November 20, 2026 around 13:45 UTC. What happened?

report.summary: Between 13:46 and 14:44 UTC on 2026-11-20 the single payment-api pod in namespace app-259 (payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12) logged eight ERROR lines 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted', with wait times rising from 1227 ms to 4840 ms and backpressure queue lengths of 5-15, i.e. its own database connection pool was saturated. INFO 'Payment processed successfully' lines interspersed (13:42, 13:59, 14:49, 15:27) show partial, not total, degradation, and no ERROR lines from this pod appear in the Loki data after 14:44. Across all namespaces present in Loki, only namespace app-259 / service payment-api produced 'pool exhausted' or any ERROR lines in the queried windows, and Loki holds no other log stream for app-259, so no database-side or caller-side log evidence exists. The underlying trigger (a slow/unresponsive database dependency holding connections, a connection leak in payment-api, or a traffic surge) cannot be determined here because Prometheus, Jaeger and the Kubernetes API all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for every query attempted, so pod status/restarts, error-rate, latency and traffic baselines are unknown rather than zero.

claims.text: In the 24h log window the only log stream in namespace app-259 is pod payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12 (job=payment-api, service=payment-api); a count_over_time by pod_name/service over the whole authorized window returned exactly that one series.

payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12 logged eight ERROR lines 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' with fields wait_time_ms and queue_length between 13:46:00Z and 14:44:00Z: 13:46 (wait 1227 ms, queue 10), 13:54 (2104 ms, 11), 14:03 (1495 ms, 8), 14:15 (2965 ms, 9), 14:19 (4005 ms, 10), 14:21 (4840 ms, 8), 14:31 (2358 ms, 15), 14:44 (3836 ms, 5).

Successful payments continued during the error period: INFO 'Payment processed successfully' with payment_id PAY-5032 at 13:42:00Z, PAY-1800 at 13:59:00Z, PAY-8206 at 14:49:00Z and PAY-4120 at 15:27:00Z.

The rolling 1-hour count of ERROR lines for pod payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12 first appears at 2026-11-20T13:47:52Z with value 1, rises to 7 by about 14:37-14:43 and falls back to 1 by 15:43, which is consistent with a single burst of errors confined to roughly 13:46-14:44.

A 6-hour rolling count by level shows the ERROR series starting at 13:47 and decaying back down while the INFO series (5-9 lines per 6h) stays present throughout the rest of the authorized window, so the pod kept logging normal activity after the burst.

Across every namespace present in Loki, the string 'pool exhausted' matched only one series for the whole authorized window: namespace app-259, service payment-api; a count by (namespace, service) over the 12:00-16:00 window likewise returned only app-259/payment-api for ERROR lines.

A count_over_time by namespace over 13:50-14:10 returned only namespace app-259 (values 1-3 lines per 10m), so Loki holds no logs from any other namespace in that slice, including no database component.

The pod was not failing every request: successful 'Payment processed successfully' lines at 13:59:00Z and 14:49:00Z bracket the error burst, so the evidence shows intermittent payment failures from connection-pool saturation, not a complete outage of payment-api.

The trigger of the pool exhaustion may be an unhealthy or slow upstream database dependency: connections were held longer over time (wait_time_ms climbing to 4840 ms) and queue lengths grew to 15 while some payments still completed. This could not be verified, because no database component emits logs into Loki and no dependency metrics or spans were retrievable.

Alternatively the pool may have been consumed from inside payment-api itself (connection leak or a long-held connection path in its own code) or by a surge in incoming payment traffic; the error text names only the pool's exhaustion and neither cause can be separated without the pod's metrics, spans or configuration, all of which were unretrievable in this Run.

Retrieve pod/deployment state and events for app-259 (restart counts, last termination reason, OOMKilled/Evicted, owner ReplicaSet) and the payment-api Prometheus series (traces_span_metrics_calls_total status_code, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds, app_payment_transactions_total) plus payment-api traces to identify which dependency was slow and whether traffic rose, then compare against a pre-13:46 baseline.

Review payment-api's database connection-pool settings (max pool size, acquire timeout) and the health of the database it connects to, since the observed failure is pool saturation with acquire waits up to 4.8 s and queued waiters up to 15.

gaps: Kubernetes API was unavailable for every query attempted (kubernetes_tabular_query, kubernetes_jq_query, kubernetes_count all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so pod phase, restart counts, last termination reason/exit code, container image, owner ReplicaSet/Deployment and events for app-259 are unknown; an OOMKilled, Evicted or restart-related component cannot be ruled in or out.

Prometheus was unavailable for every query attempted (execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_metric_names, get_label_values all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so error rate, latency (rpc_client_duration_milliseconds, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count), traffic volume (app_payment_transactions_total) and any pre-13:46 baseline for payment-api are unknown, not zero.

Jaeger was unavailable (traces_list_services and traces_search returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so there is no span-level evidence identifying which downstream dependency was slow or which callers received errors.
The database the pod could not get connections from is not identifiable from the available evidence: no other namespace or service appears in Loki, and its identity and health were not observed.
Exact cause of the pool exhaustion (dependency slowness, connection leak, or traffic surge) remains unresolved; the two hypotheses above are not verified.

The Loki ERROR-before-13:46 query (06:37:44Z-13:46:00Z) and the ERROR-after-16:00 query (16:00:00Z-06:37:44Z) both returned no_data, which shows only that those queries matched nothing; log volume is sparse (1-9 lines per hour) so absence of errors outside 13:46-14:44 is limited to what was logged and retained.
No change-history integration is available in this Run, so whether a deployment, config or scaling change preceded 13:46 could not be checked.
next_steps: Query payment-api pod/deployment status, restart counts, last termination reasons and events in namespace app-259 once the Kubernetes API is reachable.
Pull payment-api error-rate, latency and request-volume series and compare 13:00-13:45 against 13:45-15:00 to distinguish dependency slowness from a traffic surge.
Trace payment requests failing in 13:46-14:44 to the database call and check that dependency's own latency and connection metrics.
